name: Entity Attach
desc: Attaches an entity to another (player on horse, animal on leash, leach knot).

fields.name: vehicleId
fields.desc: Entity ID of the vehicle (-1 for detach)

writeup.p: S1BPacketEntityAttach is the mount and leash state channel. Opcode 0 attaches an entity to a vehicle (vehicleId -1 detaches), opcode 1 manages leash knots. The corpus server senders: EntityTrackerEntry broadcasts (0, trackedEntity, ridingEntity) when a tracked entity enters range and on mount changes (lines 166, 387), EntityPlayerMP sends (0, self, ridingEntity) when the player mounts (line 630), and EntityLiving broadcasts (1, self, leashedToEntity) on leash attach and detach (lines 991, 1016). The wire format is three ints: leash code, entityId and vehicleId.

NetHandlerPlayClient.handleEntityAttach (Memeware 7.3 bundle, line 852) resolves both entities and branches on the code. For code 0 it clears the boat empty flag for the local player, shows the 'mount.onboard' sneak hint when the player mounts a vehicle, and calls mountEntity(vehicle). For code 1 it calls setLeashedToEntity or clearLeashed on the living entity. The handler is a pure state mirror: the client applies whatever the server announces.

Zero module hits in the 8-client corpus. The only non-vanilla reference is Rise 6.x NetworkAPI, the script packet whitelist, in both 6.1.30 and 6.2.4; no module in any client branches on S1B. The structural reason: attach state is fully client-rendered and server-authoritative, and the movement exploits that involve vehicles (boat fly, entity control) act on the serverbound side, on C03 positions sent while riding and on local rider physics, not on this clientbound announcement. There is nothing to gain by intercepting a state change the client must apply verbatim.

The packet is a clientbound state mirror with no acknowledgement, so the abuse direction is server to client: a malicious server can spam attach packets to desync mount state or flip the client's ridingEntity, which corrupts the movement code path (client movement while riding uses the vehicle's physics). Anti-cheats flag vehicle abuse on the serverbound side: impossible vertical C03 deltas while the player's ridingEntity is set server-side. No cheat in the corpus interacts with this packet, and none needs to.

implementation.overview: The mount/leash packet is the one clientbound entity packet with no module consumers in the 8 clients: the only non-vanilla reference is the Rise 6.x script API whitelist. Vehicle movement exploits live entirely on the serverbound C03 side, so this announcement is left to vanilla.
implementation.server_handling: Clientbound only. The server emits it from EntityTrackerEntry on tracking start and mount/leash changes, from EntityPlayerMP when the player mounts, and from EntityLiving on leash transitions. The client applies mountEntity or setLeashedToEntity/clearLeashed and shows the onboarding hint for the local player. No validation, no rate limit, no serverbound counterpart.
implementation.protocol_notes: Three ints: code (0 = riding, 1 = leash), entityId, vehicleId (-1 or null entity for detach/clear). The boat empty flag is a client-side convenience derived from the local player's mount state, not part of the wire format. The packet is sent once per state transition, not continuously; movement while riding travels through the S14/S18 stream of the vehicle entity.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: No anticheat inspects S1B because it is clientbound. Vehicle exploits are detected from the serverbound stream: boat fly produces C03 deltas inconsistent with the mounted entity's physics, and entity-control exploits abuse C09 slot changes. The packet matters to anti-cheat designers only as the trigger for the server-side riding state that those checks key on.
implementation.general_hooks: None in the corpus. Rise 6.x scripts can receive it via the NetworkAPI whitelist (com/alan/clients/script/api/NetworkAPI.java, both versions), but no shipped module registers a handler.
implementation.client_variations: Memeware, Nekoware, Sigma, Spicy and Tenacity appear only through the vanilla NetHandlerPlayClient handler; Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 through the script API whitelist. The vanilla handler is identical across all eight bundles.
